skills.title: Living and Non-Living Things Connect
skills.description: Nature is a place where living things like plants and animals and non-living things like rocks, water, and air depend on each other. Can you sort which things are living and which are not?

skills.title: Basic Needs of Living Things
skills.description: All living things need air, water, food, heat, shelter, and space. Can you pick which things a plant or animal needs to live?

skills.title: Parts of the Human Body
skills.description: Your body has parts like eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and skin that help you sense the world. Can you match each part to where it is and what it does?

skills.title: How Body Features Meet Needs
skills.description: Plants and animals have parts like roots, leaves, fur, beaks, and legs that help them get what they need. Can you match each part to its job?

skills.title: A Healthy Environment
skills.description: A healthy place has clean air, clean water, and good food so living things can get what they need. Can you tell which places are healthy?

skills.title: Living Things Help Each Other
skills.description: Plants and animals give each other things like food and shelter. Can you match who helps whom?

skills.title: Actions for a Healthy Environment
skills.description: We can help nature by picking up litter, saving water, and planting trees. Can you pick the actions that help?

skills.title: What If Something Disappears?
skills.description: If a tree, pond, or other part of nature is lost, animals, plants, and people can be affected in different ways. Can you pick what might change?

skills.title: Energy Moves and Changes Things
skills.description: Energy is what lets something move or change. Can you pick the things that use energy to move or change?

skills.title: Using Energy at Home and School
skills.description: We use energy for lights, heating, cooking, and computers. Can you pick ways to use energy wisely, like turning off lights?

skills.title: Sources of Energy
skills.description: Energy comes from sources like the Sun, wind, water, batteries, and fuel. Can you match each source to what it is used for?

skills.title: The Sun Gives Us Energy
skills.description: The Sun warms the air, land, and water, gives us light, and helps plants grow. Can you pick what the Sun does for Earth?

skills.title: Food Is Energy
skills.description: Food gives people and animals the energy to move, grow, and play. Can you pick which things get energy from food?

skills.title: Life Without Electricity
skills.description: Without electricity, lights, fridges, and screens would stop working. Can you pick what would change for people and animals?

skills.title: Energy Resources Can Run Out
skills.description: People get energy resources like wood, oil, and water from the world around us, and many can run out. Can you tell which ones are limited?

skills.title: Energy Through the Seasons
skills.description: In winter we use heaters, and in summer we use fans. Can you match the energy we use to each season?

skills.title: Objects and Their Materials
skills.description: Objects are made of one or more materials like wood, metal, plastic, glass, and fabric. Can you match objects to what they are made of?

skills.title: Describing Objects With Senses
skills.description: We can describe objects by how they look, feel, sound, and smell, like soft, rough, shiny, or loud. Can you pick the best words for each object?

skills.title: What Objects Are For
skills.description: Every object has a job, like a cup to hold drinks or a chair to sit on. Can you match each object to its purpose?

skills.title: Structures Support a Load
skills.description: A structure is made to hold up weight, like a bridge, a table, or a bed frame. Can you pick which things are structures and what they hold?

skills.title: Material Properties and Jobs
skills.description: Materials can be strong, soft, bendy, or waterproof, which makes them good for certain jobs. Can you pick the best material for each object?

skills.title: Kinds of Fasteners
skills.description: Fasteners like buttons, zippers, nails, screws, and tape hold things together. Can you match each fastener to its use?

skills.title: Where Materials Come From
skills.description: Materials come from nature, like wood from trees, wool from sheep, and metal from rocks. Can you match each material to its source?

skills.title: Waste and How to Cut It
skills.description: People make waste like paper, food scraps, and plastic. Can you sort waste and pick ways to make less, like reusing and recycling?

skills.title: Comparing Similar Objects
skills.description: Objects with the same job can be made from different materials that come from different places and end up in different places when we are done. Can you compare them?

skills.title: Cycles Repeat
skills.description: A cycle is a set of events that happen again and again, like day and night. Can you put the events of a cycle in order?

skills.title: Earth and the Sun
skills.description: Earth spins to make day and night and travels around the Sun to make seasons. Can you pick what causes day, night, and seasons?

skills.title: Sunlight and Heat Change
skills.description: The Sun gives different amounts of light and heat during the day and in each season. Can you tell when it is brightest and warmest?

skills.title: Weather in the Four Seasons
skills.description: Winter, spring, summer, and fall have different weather, rain, snow, and temperatures. Can you match the weather to each season?

skills.title: Living Things and Seasons
skills.description: Animals and plants change with the seasons, like trees losing leaves, birds flying south, or bears sleeping. Can you match each change to its season?

skills.title: People Get Ready for Seasons
skills.description: People change clothes, homes, and food as the day and seasons change. Can you pick what people do for each kind of weather?

skills.title: Seasons and Outdoor Fun
skills.description: Some outdoor fun, like skating or swimming, fits certain seasons, and inventions like indoor rinks let us play all year. Can you match activities to seasons and inventions?

skills.title: How Changes Affect Our World
skills.description: Day and season changes affect towns, nature, and animals, like snow closing roads or ponds freezing. Can you pick the effects?
